Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some wallets are purses.

Some purses are bags.

All bags are suitcases.

**Conclusions:**

I. No wallet is a suitcase.

II. Some purses are suitcases.

III. All wallets being bags is a possibility.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
All conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
From the given statements, the Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bbb3bcd5f835cc13e239f898c0f8fa57e588730b6d76bc3819170ba2fe46552.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

I. No wallet is a suitcase → Does not follow → From the given information we have no evidence that supports the relation between wallet and suitcase and the diagram also does not depict and connection therefore the conclusion does not follow.

II. Some purses are suitcases → Follow → As 'some purses are bags' and 'all bags are suitcases' so we can see a direct relation that suggests that some purses are suitcases and we can see the same in the diagram thus the conclusion follows.

III. All wallets being bags is a possibility → Follow → As all the number of wallets are purses and all the same part is related to bags so there is a slight possibility that this conclusion is true so we can say that the conclusion follows.

So only conclusion II and III follow.

Hence **the correct answer is option 4)**
